text:
carla: Running a perf sweep on staging MI210 pool. p95 jumps between seqlen 460-500. Suspect kernel lookup gap causing fallback to generic matmul.

noah: can you paste the small trace? a one-line snippet is fine.

carla: here's the relevant serving log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] kernel_index: model=redwood-7b, op=matmul_bias, seq=476, device=mi210
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] kernel_index: candidates=[tiled_fp16_seq=448, tiled_fp16_seq=512]
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] kernel_index: exact_match=false
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] router.choice: route=rocm_generic_matmul (est_overhead_ms=3.2)
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] exec.annot: path=rocm_generic_matmul gpu
[2026-03-18T01:15:01Z] kv_cache: hit=0.78 avg_prefix_len=90
```

ying: looks like our router enforces exact seq registration. strange that it didn't pick seq=512 tiled even though it's listed as candidate.

noah: maybe the metadata flags on the seq=512 kernel mark it as "non-compatible" for matmul_bias fused op? we had that guard for some fused kernels after the quantization change.

ops-bot: ci: kernel-availability-check --pool mi210 --model redwood-7b --seq 460..500 queued

carla: two mitigation ideas: (1) introduce a nearest-tiling policy that picks the smallest compatible tile >= seqlen (if within tolerance), with a penalty estimate; (2) schedule a targeted build to produce explicit seq tiles for 464/480/496.

ying: +1 for nearest-tiling as short term. we should annotate responses with a routing_hint so downstream metrics can split by routed-vs-exact.

noah: also want a safety parity probe: run N samples, compare outputs vs exact-tile CPU reference; if difference > eps we rollback for that kernel+model combo.

carla: prototyped config I ran locally: 
```
route_policy: nearest_tile
seq_tolerance: 24
penalty_ms: 1.1
annotate_routing: true
```
Results: reduced gpu_generic routes from 38 -> 5 in a 300-run bench, p95 down ~2.8ms -> 0.9ms. parity diffs within float16 eps for this model.

bench-bot: bench report uploaded: s3://redwood-staging/bench/mi210/1765432101/route_report.json (summary p50:12.3ms p95:18.9ms before; p50:11.8 p95:12.7 after)

ying: nice. couple followups: (a) controller should expose effective_seqlen after kv/masking so router sees real distribution; (b) router should keep a short TTL cache of recently used nearest-tile mappings per pool to avoid repeated lookup cost.

noah: agree. I'll add the seqlen histogram metric (per-pool, 1m buckets) and a router hook that auto-increases seq_tolerance if gap rate > 2% sustained for 2 windows.

carla: noted. also found edge-case: int8 kernels exist for some tiles — we could prefer int8 when nearest-tile is missing if parity probe passes, often faster than generic fp16 on GPU.

ying: be conservative with int8; add numerical checks and opt-in via rollout flag. don't want subtle hallucination regressions.

ops-bot: deploy-plan check: nearest-tiling mode marked canary=true for pool=mi210 (status: ok)

noah: plan checklist:
- add controller seqlen histograms (telemetry)
- enable nearest_tile canary on mi210 for 12h
- queue kernel build for explicit tiles (long term)
- add parity CI for nearest_tile and int8 fallback

carla: opening PRs now and will attach flamegraphs/summary. will post bench IDs here when CI finishes. react with :eyes: if you can review quickly.

ying: will review router PR. if canary shows any regression we can auto-revert with rollout policy.

noah: sounds good. Thanks all.
